properties.decision:
SETTLED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-15: "allow VERIFIES → Constraint". OPTION (a) of the four below.

WHAT WAS BUILT, the same day: `schema/verify.yaml`'s `to:` list becomes `[Capability, Requirement, Artifact, Component, DesignRule, Constraint]`. The schema is compiled in via `include_str!`, so the rebuild carries it.

PROVEN THROUGH THE PATH THAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN — the importer, not a unit assertion. A document holding `VERIFIES ver:latency_gate -> con:latency` now imports (exit 0, '2 node(s) and 1 edge(s)'). ⭐ AND THE COUNTERWEIGHT RAN IN THE SAME BREATH: a document holding `VERIFIES -> Project` is STILL REFUSED, with the same precise message. THE LIST DISCRIMINATES; IT WAS NOT QUIETLY WIDENED.

Pinned by `crates/reflow2-core/tests/verifies_reaches_a_constraint.rs`, 2 cases, MUTATION-CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: removing `Constraint` fails the case and leaves the counterweight passing; restoring the pre-2026-08-08 `to: \"*\"` passes the case and FAILS THE COUNTERWEIGHT — which is what proves the counterweight is doing work rather than agreeing for free.

⚠️ PROJECT IS DELIBERATELY STILL OUT, AND DEV_STORYFLOW'S EXPORT THEREFORE STILL WILL NOT IMPORT. Their file carries TWO illegal edges — one Constraint, one Project — and only the Constraint half was ruled on. A Verification that verifies a whole Project reads as a modelling slip rather than a need, but nobody has decided, and this decision deliberately does not decide it for them. Their backup remains unrestorable until either that edge is migrated by them or Project is admitted here.

WHY (a) OVER THE OTHERS: (b) migrating the edge away would reshape a real design to satisfy a validator, which is the failure `rule:never_shape_a_field_to_satisfy_an_instrument` names and which their own reporter warned against — 'the question should be asked before anyone deletes data to satisfy a validator'. (c) re-deriving across every known graph settles this instance without settling the rule, and can still be done later. (d) restoring the wildcard discards the reason the enumeration was added, which is recorded in the file and was a real gain: it made 'which of my rules have no detector?' an askable question.

THE ORIGINAL QUESTION, PRESERVED so a later reader sees what was weighed:

A Constraint is 'a limit or rule the design MUST respect' — a latency budget, a mass cap, 'no PII leaves the device'. Asking whether a limit HOLDS is the most natural thing anyone would want to check about it, and it is exactly what `budget_report` answers arithmetically for the numeric case. A Verification is how this design records that something was CHECKED. Refusing to connect them said a limit may be stated and computed but never independently verified. AND THE ASYMMETRY WAS ODD ON ITS FACE: `DesignRule` was already in the list, and `unverified_enforced_rule` exists precisely so a gate-blocking rule owes a passing check. A Constraint is the DesignRule's sibling — the imposed limit beside the chosen one — and nothing in the schema explained why they were split.

HOW IT AROSE: `ver:side_e_slo_gate_unwired_2026_08_09` VERIFIES `con:side_e_perf_slos_are_enforced_nowhere` in dev_storyflow — a check measuring whether a performance constraint is actually enforced. The 2026-08-08 narrowing of `VERIFIES` from `*` to an enumeration derived its list from a census that found five types at 95/27/13/2/1 edges and MISSED TWO CARRYING ONE EDGE EACH. See `fact:defect-a-schema-narrowing-orphaned-live-edges-and-no-export-is-ever-imported`.

NOT SETTLED BY THIS, and left open on purpose: whether `Project` belongs; whether the list should be re-derived across all three known designs; and whether any detector should READ the new edge — admitting it makes the claim expressible, and nothing yet computes anything from it.
properties.name: A Verification MAY verify a Constraint — a check that measures whether a limit holds is a real modelling need, and Project stays out
properties.rationale: Recorded as his ruling rather than as an agent's fix because it is a schema change with real data on both sides: the wrong answer either destroys a legitimate edge or admits everything. He chose the option that repairs the design without touching anyone's data. The Project half was deliberately NOT bundled with it — the reporter who found both asked for them to be judged separately, and folding them together would have settled a second question nobody put.
